Deletes a backup from the panel as well as the remote source where it is currently
being stored.

get.description:
Download the backup for a given server instance. For daemon local files, the file
will be streamed back through the Panel. For AWS S3 files, a signed URL will be generated
which the user is redirected to.

put.description: Updates the name of a backup for a server instance.

post.description: Toggles the lock status of a given backup for a server.

Handles restoring a backup by making a request to the daemon instance telling it
to begin the process of finding (or downloading) the backup and unpacking it
over the server files.

If the "truncate" flag is passed through in this request then all the
files that currently exist on the server will be deleted before restoring.
Otherwise, the archive will simply be unpacked over the existing files.

get.description:
Generates a one-time token that is sent along in every websocket call to the Daemon.
This is a signed JWT that the Daemon then uses to verify the user's identity, and
allows us to continually renew this token and avoid users maintaining sessions wrongly,
as well as ensure that user's only perform actions they're allowed to.

files.description: Files and directories to put in the archive.

extension.description: Archive format to write. Defaults to `tar.gz`.

root.description: Directory the new folder is created in, relative to the server root.

files.description: Files and directories to delete. Directories are removed with everything inside them.

items.description: Name of a file or directory, relative to `root`.

url.description: URL the file is downloaded from.

directory.description: Directory the file is saved in, relative to the server root.

filename.description: Name to save the file under. Taken from the URL when left empty.

use_header.description: Take the file name from the response's `Content-Disposition` header instead of the URL.

foreground.description: Wait for the download to finish before responding rather than running it in the background.

root.description: Directory the files live in, relative to the server root.

files.description: Files and directories to rename. Renaming across directories moves the file.

to.description: New name of the file, relative to `root`.

from.description: Current name of the file, relative to `root`.

truncate.description: Delete everything in the server directory before the backup is unpacked.

command.description: Command to write to the server's console, without a trailing newline.

signal.description: Power action to send. `kill` stops the container immediately and may lose unsaved data.

docker_image.description: Docker image the server container is built from. Must be one of the images the server's egg offers.

description.description: Note describing what the key is for.

allowed_ips.description: IP addresses the key may be used from. Leave empty to allow any address.

items.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address the key may be used from.

name.description: Name for the backup. A timestamped name is generated when this is left empty.

is_locked.description: Lock the backup so it cannot be deleted or rotated out until it is unlocked. Only applied when the caller has the delete-backup permission; ignored otherwise.

ignored.description: Newline separated list of paths to leave out of the backup, in the same format as `.gitignore`.

database.description: Name of the database to create. The final name is prefixed with the server ID, and must not already be in use by this server.

remote.description: Addresses the database user may connect from. Use `%` to allow any address.

name.description: Name the key is listed under in the Panel.

public_key.description: The public half of the SSH key, in OpenSSH format.

name.description: Name the schedule is shown under in the Panel.

is_active.description: Whether the schedule runs at all. Inactive schedules keep their settings but never fire.

only_when_online.description: Skip the run when the server is not online at the scheduled time.

minute.description: Minute field of the cron expression, such as `0` or `*`.

hour.description: Hour field of the cron expression.

day_of_month.description: Day of month field of the cron expression.

month.description: Month field of the cron expression.

time_offset.description: Seconds to wait after the previous task finishes before this one runs.

sequence_id.description: Position of the task within the schedule. Tasks run in ascending order.

continue_on_failure.description: Keep running the remaining tasks even if this one fails.

notes.description: Note describing what the allocation is used for. Send `null` to clear it.

day_of_week.description: Day of week field of the cron expression, where `0` is Sunday.

permissions.description: Permissions the subuser is granted on this server. Permissions left out of this list are revoked.
